facts.text: On this date in 1920, the 19th Amendment was certified, giving American women the right to vote — 144 years after the Declaration of Independence.
On this date in 1883, Krakatoa's eruption was heard 4,800 km away in Australia, the loudest sound in recorded human history.
More people live inside a circle drawn around Dhaka, Bangladesh than in the entire United States west of the Mississippi River.
Monaco has a higher density of millionaires per capita than any nation on Earth — roughly one in three residents qualifies.
The Philippines is the only country in Asia where the majority of the population is Christian, a legacy of 333 years of Spanish colonial rule.
On Aug 26, 1346, Edward III paid his mercenary crossbowmen in silver coin minted from wool taxes — medieval England ran its wars on sheep.
On Aug 26, 1920, women gained the vote in the US. The 19th Amendment unlocked an estimated $3 trillion in long-run consumer spending power that markets had simply never priced.
The NYSE's famously chaotic trading floor employs fewer people today than a single mid-sized Subway franchise — most volume is routed through servers in Mahwah, New Jersey.
Berkshire Hathaway's Class A share has never been split. One share now costs more than the median American home, by design — Buffett wanted owners, not traders.

The Dutch East India Company paid dividends for 200 consecutive years, financed wars, minted its own coins, and maintained a standing army. It remains the largest corporation in history by inflation-adjusted valuation.
On this date in 1743, Antoine Lavoisier was born. He would later prove that burning consumes oxygen rather than releasing phlogiston, dismantling a theory chemists had trusted for a century.
On August 26, 1920, women gained U.S. voting rights — the same year a solar storm so powerful it set telegraph wires on fire was largely forgotten beside it.
Your skeleton is not static scaffolding. Every decade, your body replaces nearly all its bone mass, rebuilding itself from calcium pulled from your own blood.
A neutron star packs more mass than the Sun into a sphere the size of a city. A single teaspoon of its material would weigh roughly a billion tons on Earth.
Mantis shrimp see with 16 types of color receptors — humans have 3 — yet process color less accurately. More sensors, paradoxically, means less discrimination.
On this day in 1920, the 19th Amendment was certified, giving American women the right to vote — 144 years after the nation declared all men created equal.
Cleopatra lived closer in time to the Moon landing than to the construction of the Great Pyramid. The pyramid is simply that old.
On this day in 1883, Krakatoa erupted so loudly that people heard it 4,800 km away in Australia — the farthest sound ever documented in recorded history.
The University of Oxford was already 300 years old when the Aztec Empire was founded. Europe's oldest university predates what most people picture as 'ancient' Mesoamerica.
Nintendo was founded in 1889, when Grover Cleveland was president and the Eiffel Tower had just opened. It sold playing cards for nearly a century before it touched a video game.
Sonder (n.): the realization that every passerby has a life as vivid and complex as your own. Coined by John Koenig in 2012, it spread so fast linguists debate whether invented words can go native.
Hiraeth (Welsh, n.): a longing for a home that may never have existed — or can never be revisited. English has no single word for it, which says something about English.
On this day in 1743, the French Academy officially admitted 'café' into its dictionary, reluctantly blessing a word coffeehouses had already made immortal.
Vellichor (n.): the strange wistfulness of a used bookshop. Also from Koenig's Dictionary of Obscure Sorrows — proof that naming a feeling is halfway to owning it.
On this day in 1920, the 19th Amendment was certified into law. The word 'suffrage' descends from Latin suffragium — a voting tablet, a broken tile, a shard of voice cast into the count.
On this date in 2012, Coinbase officially launched its exchange service — before that, buying Bitcoin in the US meant navigating Mt. Gox from Japan or peer-to-peer IRC channels.
On August 26, 2021, Ethereum's EIP-1559 had already burned over 100,000 ETH in its first three weeks, making ETH structurally deflationary under high network load for the first time.
Bitcoin's timelock opcode, OP_CHECKLOCKTIMEVERIFY, sat unused in the codebase for years before BIP 65 activated it in 2015 — the feature existed before anyone had permission to use it.

The DAO hack in 2016 didn't exploit Solidity — it exploited a reentrancy pattern the auditors understood but considered acceptable, draining 3.6M ETH through a withdrawal function called recursively before balances updated.
Satoshi's original whitepaper never uses the word 'blockchain' — the phrase 'chain of blocks' appears, but 'blockchain' as a compound noun was popularized later by the broader community.
On this date in 2012, Alex Krizhevsky submitted AlexNet to ImageNet — the 10.8-point top-5 error gap over second place was so large that reviewers assumed a reporting error.
Today in 2016, Google announced it had retrained its entire production neural machine translation system from scratch in under a week, replacing eight years of phrase-based engineering.
GPT-4's training run is estimated to have consumed more FLOPs than all human arithmetic performed in recorded history — combined.

The transformer architecture, now the backbone of virtually every frontier model, was originally a side project aimed at speeding up Google Translate. Attention Is All You Need was rejected from one workshop before publication.
Chinchilla (2022) showed that most large language models prior to it were simultaneously overtrained on compute and undertrained on data — including GPT-3, by a significant margin.
